title: Suriya's 'Karuppu' Smashes Past ₹100 Crore to Become His Biggest Film Ever
excerpt: The Tamil action-thriller has crossed ₹150 crore worldwide in just five days, with Trisha Krishnan's return proving that South Indian cinema's box office dominance is no fluke
body:
Five days. ₹150 crore worldwide. And a career record that nobody saw coming quite this fast.

Suriya is having the biggest moment of his three-decade career. His fantasy action-thriller Karuppu, directed by RJ Balaji and co-starring Trisha Krishnan, has bulldozed through box office records since its May 15 release, becoming his first film to cross the ₹100 crore mark domestically — and it's showing no signs of slowing down.

The Numbers Are Staggering

Karuppu opened with a solid ₹15.5 crore on Day 1, then caught fire. Day 2 brought in ₹24.15 crore, Day 3 surged to ₹28.35 crore (a Sunday boost that signaled genuine mass appeal), and even the traditionally weaker Monday delivered ₹14.30 crore — a controlled drop that analysts consider healthy for a mid-range budget Tamil film.

The five-day India net stands at approximately ₹95 crore, with the India gross touching ₹110 crore. Overseas collections have added another ₹40+ crore, pushing the worldwide total past the ₹150 crore mark.

To put this in perspective: Karuppu has already surpassed Singam 2 (₹122.8 crore worldwide, 2013) to become Suriya's highest-grossing film of all time. It also overtook 24 (₹108.9 crore) in just three days. At its current pace, industry analysts project a lifetime collection of ₹200+ crore — which would make it the top-grossing Tamil film of 2026.

Why It's Working

The Suriya-Trisha pairing is, frankly, one of Tamil cinema's most bankable combinations — they last shared screen space in the Aaytha Ezhuthu era, and the reunion has clearly tapped into nostalgia and genuine star chemistry. RJ Balaji, better known as a comedian and talk-show host, has proven himself as a director who can handle large-scale action-drama, blending mythological elements with contemporary storytelling.

Critics have praised Suriya's intense performance and the film's first half, though some have noted the second half loses momentum. But audiences are voting with their wallets: on BookMyShow, Karuppu became the second-highest-selling Tamil film of 2026, surpassing even Thalapathy Vijay's Leo with 690,000 ticket sales on Day 2 alone — a total of 1.46 million tickets in just 48 hours.

The Diaspora Angle

For the Tamil diaspora — particularly in the US, UK, Singapore, and the Gulf — Karuppu's release has been an event. Tamil-language screenings in major NRI hubs like Edison (NJ), Sunnyvale, Dallas, and London reported near-sellout shows over the opening weekend. International collections accounted for roughly 27% of the worldwide gross, a proportion that underscores how Tamil cinema's audience is no longer confined to Tamil Nadu.

What's especially notable is that Karuppu achieved this without the typical Hindi dubbing push that many South Indian blockbusters now rely on. This is a Tamil film performing like a pan-India release purely on the strength of its regional fanbase and overseas diaspora.

What It Means for Tamil Cinema in 2026

Tamil cinema has had a rocky post-pandemic stretch. Outside the stratospheric success of a few juggernauts (Jailer, Leo), the industry struggled with inconsistent theatrical returns. Karuppu's blockbuster run offers a genuine morale boost — proof that a well-executed star vehicle with strong content can still pack theatres without relying on franchise IP or multi-language releases.

For Suriya, at 50, it's a triumphant answer to anyone who questioned whether he could still anchor a ₹100 crore opener. He can. He just did.

What's Next

Karuppu enters its second week facing competition from Drishyam 3 (releasing May 21) and the Hindi market's ongoing hits. The key question: can weekday collections sustain enough momentum to reach ₹200 crore? If the Monday hold is any indicator, the answer is yes.
